Add an ORDER BY event_time clause to the query so that Athena can skip row groups that fall outside the sort range
List only the three needed columns in the SELECT clause instead of selecting every column with SELECT *
Replace the date filter with a filter on a string-formatted copy of event_time so the comparison is done as text

stem: A Lambda function in a VPC loads records into Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. Security policy now forbids long-lived database passwords anywhere, including in secret stores, and requires that database access be granted through IAM policies. Which approach fits?

Store the password in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation every 30 days and let the function fetch it at start
Restrict the database security group to the function's security group and use a database user that has no password
Join the DB instance to AWS Directory Service and have the function authenticate to PostgreSQL with Kerberos tickets

stem: Producer Lambda functions and consumer ECS tasks use an Amazon MSK cluster. The team wants clients to authenticate with their existing IAM roles and to control which roles can write or read each topic in IAM policies, without managing usernames, passwords, certificates or Kafka ACLs. Leave the cluster unauthenticated inside the VPC and restrict access to the brokers using security group rules
Enable SASL/SCRAM authentication with credentials stored in Secrets Manager and set Kafka ACLs for each topic
Enable mutual TLS with AWS Private CA certificates for each client and authorize topic access with Kafka ACLs

stem: A team registered its S3 data lake location with AWS Lake Formation and granted SELECT on one table only to the analyst role. choices.text: The tables have no LF-Tags assigned yet; attach LF-Tags to every table so Lake Formation starts enforcing the tag-based access

stem: A team enabled server-side encryption on an Amazon Kinesis data stream using a customer managed KMS key. Immediately afterward, producers fail with KMS access denied errors on PutRecords, and consumers can no longer read records. Which TWO permissions must be added to fix this? (Select TWO)

kms:Encrypt on the customer managed key for the consumer roles so they can re-encrypt records they read
kms:Decrypt on the customer managed key for the IAM roles used by the consumer applications and Lambda
kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion on the key for the stream owner so that old data keys can be retired periodically

stem: Auditors ask a data platform team to prove that the CloudTrail log files stored in S3 for the past year were not modified or deleted after CloudTrail delivered them. Which capability provides this proof MOST directly?

choices.text: Encrypt the log files with SSE-KMS using a customer managed key so only authorized principals can decrypt the logs
Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation and verify the digest files with the aws cloudtrail validate-logs command

Enable S3 Versioning on the log bucket so every earlier version of each log file remains available to compare with

stem: A company with 60 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations must capture API activity for all current and future accounts in one place. Administrators in member accounts must not be able to stop the logging or alter the delivered log files. Which TWO actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Send each account's trail to CloudWatch Logs in that same account and keep the log group retention set to ten years
Set up an AWS Config aggregator in the management account that collects configuration records from all the accounts
Deploy a separate CloudTrail trail in each member account with CloudFormation StackSets managed by account admins
Create an organization trail from the management account so that it applies to all current and future member accounts
Deliver the trail to an S3 bucket in a dedicated log archive account with S3 Object Lock in compliance mode enabled

stem: A retailer and a media company want to measure how many of their customers overlap and compare campaign reach. Neither company may see the other's row-level customer records, results must only be aggregates above a minimum group size, and each company's data should stay in its own AWS account. Which service fits?

choices.text: AWS Clean Rooms with an aggregation analysis rule that sets minimum aggregation thresholds on the join columns
AWS Lake Formation cross-account table sharing with column-level grants that exclude direct identifier columns
An S3 bucket policy granting the media company read access to a daily hashed export of the retailer's customers
Amazon Redshift data sharing from the retailer to the media company with a view limited to the joinable columns

stem: A data lake stores customer events in S3 as Apache Iceberg tables queried with Athena. Under GDPR, a customer's erasure request requires that their rows are physically removed from storage within 30 days, not just hidden from queries. Which process meets this requirement?

choices.text: Create a Lake Formation row filter that excludes the customer's ID so that no analyst query ever returns their rows
Run an Athena DELETE for the customer's rows, then OPTIMIZE to rewrite data files and VACUUM to expire old snapshots
Enable S3 Versioning on the bucket and delete the Parquet objects that contain the customer's rows along with others
Add an S3 Lifecycle rule that expires every object older than 30 days so that the customer's data ages out naturally

stem: An EMR Spark job and a GPU training fleet run in one Availability Zone and repeatedly read millions of small intermediate files through the S3 API. The files can be regenerated if lost, and per-request latency now dominates job run time. The team wants to keep using the S3 API. Which storage choice fits BEST?

choices.text: An Amazon EFS One Zone file system mounted on every node so that the jobs can read the small files with low file-system latency
An S3 bucket that uses the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class so that frequently read files stay in the Frequent Access tier
An S3 Express One Zone directory bucket created in the same Availability Zone as the compute that reads and writes the files
An S3 Standard bucket with S3 Transfer Acceleration turned on so that each GET request is served through the nearest edge location

stem: A payments company must detect fraud rings by finding accounts that share devices, cards or IP addresses up to five hops apart, and each check must return in well under a second while a payment is being authorized. The relationships change constantly. Which data store fits BEST?

choices.text: Amazon Neptune storing accounts, devices, cards and IPs as vertices and edges, queried with openCypher or Gremlin traversals
Amazon Redshift with recursive common table expressions that walk the relationship table from the account to five levels deep
Amazon OpenSearch Service with nested documents for each account and terms queries that match shared device and card values
Amazon DynamoDB with an adjacency-list design, where the application issues one Query per hop and merges the results in code

stem: A company runs a self-managed Apache Cassandra cluster on EC2 for a time-series application. Operations staff spend most of their time on node repairs, patching and capacity planning. choices.text: Migrate the tables to Amazon DocumentDB and use its compatibility layer so that the application keeps its query model
Migrate the tables to Amazon DynamoDB and use the DynamoDB SDK because its partition and sort keys match Cassandra keys
Move the Cassandra cluster onto larger EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group so that nodes are replaced when they fail
Migrate the tables to Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) and point the existing CQL drivers at the service endpoint

stem: An AWS Glue crawler runs every hour over an S3 bucket that holds hundreds of millions of objects. New files arrive in both new and existing partition folders, and newly added columns must appear in the Data Catalog. Each crawl now takes hours because the crawler lists the whole bucket. choices.text: Change the recrawl policy to crawl new folders only, so that each run lists and processes only the folders created since the last crawl
Set the crawler to use S3 event notifications delivered to an SQS queue, so that each run processes only the objects that changed
Split the bucket into several crawlers with exclusion patterns, and run all of those crawlers on the same hourly schedule in parallel
Lower the crawler sample size so that only a few files in each leaf folder are read, which shortens the schema inference for the bucket

stem: An Athena table has over one million partitions keyed by event_date and customer_id, where customer IDs are arbitrary strings added daily. Some queries filter only on a customer_id and others only on a date range, and query planning alone takes a long time. The S3 layout must not change. Which change BEST reduces planning time?

choices.text: Enable Athena query result reuse on the workgroup so that repeated queries skip planning and read the cached query results
Run MSCK REPAIR TABLE after every load so that the Data Catalog always has the full and current list of all table partitions
Create AWS Glue partition indexes on customer_id and on event_date, and enable partition filtering in the table properties
Configure partition projection with a date range for event_date and the enum type for customer_id listing all existing values

stem: A producer account governs its S3 data lake with AWS Lake Formation, including column-level permissions on a sales database. Analysts in a consumer account must query some tables with Athena, and the column restrictions must still apply without copying data. Which TWO steps are required? (Select TWO)

In both accounts, enable S3 Cross-Region Replication so that the consumer receives a synchronized copy of the tables
In the consumer account, run a Glue crawler over the producer's S3 paths so that local tables point to the same data

In the producer account, grant Lake Formation permissions on the selected tables and columns to the consumer account ID

stem: Analysts write Athena queries that join a large Parquet fact table with several dimension tables, and they often list the tables in an inefficient order. choices.text: Add partition projection to each dimension table so that Athena calculates their partitions instead of calling the catalog
Convert all the dimension tables from Parquet to gzip-compressed JSON so that each one of them is read as a single file
Generate column statistics for the tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog so that the Athena cost-based optimizer can use them
Enable Athena query result reuse so that queries with the same text return cached results for the configured maximum age

stem: A Glue crawler runs over S3 folders containing application logs in a custom line format such as "2026-09-29T10:15:02Z INFO [orders] user=42 latency=87ms". Create a custom grok classifier with a pattern that matches the log line format and add it to the crawler's classifiers
Increase the crawler sample size so that more files in each folder are inspected before a built-in classifier is picked
Add a custom CSV classifier with a space delimiter, because the built-in CSV classifier cannot parse the log lines

stem: A data lake bucket stores several million objects, mostly 5 to 200 MB. Some datasets go untouched for months and then are suddenly read heavily when a new model is trained, and nobody can predict which ones. The team wants to lower storage cost without retrieval fees or lifecycle rules to maintain. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Add a lifecycle rule that moves every object to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 90 days to reduce the storage price
Add a lifecycle rule that moves every object to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days and back to S3 Standard when it is read
Store all the objects in S3 One Zone-IA from the beginning, because it has the lowest price for instantly readable data
Store the objects in S3 Intelligent-Tiering so that S3 moves each object between access tiers based on its actual access

stem: Financial records in an S3 bucket must be retained for 7 years and protected from deletion or overwrite by engineers and pipelines. However, a small compliance team must be able to remove objects that were uploaded in error, after an approval process. Which configuration fits BEST?

choices.text: Place a legal hold on every object as it arrives, and give pipeline roles permission to remove legal holds whenever needed

Enable Object Lock in governance mode with a 7-year default retention, and grant only the compliance role bypass permission

stem: An auditor needs 40 TB of log archives, about 3 million objects in the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class, restored for analysis. Use S3 Batch Operations with a manifest of the objects and a Restore job that uses the Bulk retrieval tier

stem: An Athena table over Parquet files in S3 is registered in the Glue Data Catalog as a standard Hive-style table. Rename and drop the columns directly in the Glue Data Catalog table definition, and let Athena map them onto the old files

stem: A data lake team registered an S3 location with AWS Lake Formation and granted SELECT on a single column of a table to an analyst role. Analysts still see every column of the table when they query it with Athena. Nothing else grants the role access. What should the team check FIRST?

stem: A platform team wants to let each data engineering team create its own IAM roles for Glue jobs, but no team may ever grant a role more than access to its own S3 prefix and the Glue Data Catalog, even if a team writes a policy with wildcards. Which control fits BEST?

stem: A team enabled cross-Region snapshot copy from an encrypted Amazon Redshift cluster in eu-west-1 to eu-central-1 for disaster recovery. The copy of automated snapshots never appears in the destination Region. Which missing step is the MOST likely cause?

stem: A Glue job loads customer records that include free-form columns which may contain email addresses and phone numbers. The data team must keep the records joinable on the sensitive value across datasets without exposing the clear value to analysts. Which transform fits BEST?

stem: A security team reviews how automatic rotation works on a symmetric customer managed AWS KMS key that protects objects in several S3 buckets. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The rotation period is fixed at exactly one year and cannot be changed to a shorter or longer number of days
Rotation must be switched on separately in each bucket's default encryption settings, because the S3 service performs the key rotation
The key ID and ARN stay the same after rotation, so applications and bucket settings that reference the key need no change
Rotation immediately re-encrypts every existing object in the buckets with the new key material, which can take several days
Older key material is kept, so data encrypted before the rotation can still be decrypted without re-encrypting it

stem: Auditors ask the data platform team to show which IAM principals read data from which Lake Formation governed tables during the last quarter. Analysts query the tables through Athena, and CloudTrail management events are already delivered to S3. Which evidence source answers the question BEST?

choices.text: The Athena query history in the console, which keeps every query text from every workgroup for at least two years by default
S3 Storage Lens activity metrics for the data lake bucket, which list the individual IAM principals that read each table's files
AWS Config configuration history for the Glue tables, which records every read operation and the identity that performed it
CloudTrail events recorded when Lake Formation vends temporary credentials, which name the calling principal and the table involved

stem: A team turned on S3 server access logging for a sensitive bucket and named a separate log bucket as the target, in the same Region and account. Several days later no log objects have ever appeared. The log bucket uses default encryption with SSE-KMS and a customer managed key. What is the MOST likely cause?

choices.text: The log bucket sits in the same Region as the source, and S3 requires the target bucket to be in a different Region for logs
The log bucket's default encryption uses SSE-KMS, but server access log delivery supports only SSE-S3 default encryption on the target
The source bucket has versioning turned on, and S3 does not create access logs for any bucket that stores several object versions
The log bucket lacks a lifecycle rule, and S3 does not begin delivering logs until an expiration rule has been added there

stem: Compliance requires that the exact SQL text and the IAM identity for every Amazon Athena query be kept for two years, in a store the analysts cannot alter. Athena query history in the console only goes back a short time. Which solution fits BEST?

choices.text: Turn on S3 server access logs for the Athena results bucket, which store the SQL that produced each results file
Ask analysts to export their query history from the console each month and upload the files to a shared S3 bucket
Deliver CloudTrail events to a protected S3 bucket, where StartQueryExecution calls record the query string and caller
Enable Athena workgroup metrics in CloudWatch, which store the complete query text and the caller identity for each query

stem: A team enabled audit logging on an Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster with delivery to Amazon S3. Connection logs and user logs appear, but the auditors also need the full text of every SQL statement executed, and no such log exists. What is the MOST likely fix?

choices.text: Set the enable_user_activity_logging parameter to true in the cluster's custom parameter group, which adds the user activity log to audit logging
Raise the wlm_query_slot_count parameter of the queue, since statement text is logged only for queries that use more than one slot
Attach the AWSCloudTrailReadOnlyAccess policy to the cluster's IAM role, so that the cluster starts writing statement text to the trail
Create a database user named audit and grant it SELECT on the system tables, so that every executed statement is copied to it as a log

stem: A company keeps employee records in S3 where each employee has an identifier in the form EMP followed by seven digits, with the words "employee id" nearby. Amazon Macie's managed data identifiers do not recognize this format. The company wants Macie sensitive data discovery jobs to report objects that contain it. What should the team create?

choices.text: A Glue crawler classifier with a grok pattern for the format, which Macie reads through the Data Catalog before it starts a job
An S3 Inventory report that lists every object whose key contains the text EMP, which Macie then uses as the sensitive list
An Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognizer trained on a few samples, which Macie calls automatically during every discovery job
A custom data identifier in Macie defined by a regular expression for the format, with optional keywords and a proximity distance

stem: A financial firm must store trade confirmations in Amazon S3 for seven years so that no user, including the account root user, can delete or overwrite any object version before the retention period ends, and regulators must be able to rely on that guarantee. Which configuration fits BEST?

choices.text: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode, with a seven-year default retention period applied to the bucket
S3 Versioning with MFA delete turned on, so that deletes need a hardware token held by the root user
A bucket policy that denies s3:DeleteObject to every principal except a break-glass role in the account
S3 Object Lock in governance mode, with a seven-year default retention period applied to the bucket

stem: A versioned S3 bucket holds customer exports. To meet a 90-day retention policy, a lifecycle rule expires current objects after 90 days. The exports disappear from listings, yet storage costs and the data volume stay almost the same, and auditors find old customer data still recoverable. What should the team add?

choices.text: A lifecycle rule on the bucket that enables S3 Intelligent-Tiering so that unused objects are removed after 90 days of no access
An S3 Inventory configuration that lists all versions weekly, which lets S3 remove any version that is older than 90 days
A rule with noncurrent version expiration so that previous versions are permanently deleted a few days after they become noncurrent
A rule that transitions the current versions to S3 Glacier Deep Archive at day 91 so that the old data is stored more cheaply

stem: A contact center stores thousands of call transcripts as text files in S3. The transcripts contain names, addresses and card numbers in free text. Before analysts explore them in Athena, the company must remove the personal data, and they need the transcripts to remain readable text. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: An S3 Lifecycle rule that moves transcripts with card numbers to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and blocks their reading in Athena
An Amazon Comprehend PII redaction job on the transcripts that writes new files with detected entities masked or replaced by their type
An Athena view with a column mask on the transcript column, which hides the sensitive words from analysts at query time
An Amazon Macie sensitive data discovery job on the bucket, which redacts the detected values inside every transcript it scans
